How are the Syriac passive/reflexive stems formed?
opts: With the prefix ʾet- on the Peal, Paael or Aphel

q: Which stem is the passive of the Peal?
opts: That is the passive of the Paael.
That is the passive of the Aphel.
The Aphel is causative and active.

q: Why does the passive of šaddar appear as ʾeštaddar rather than ʾetšaddar?
opts: Before a sibilant (s, š, ṣ, z) the t of ʾet- swaps places with it (metathesis).
The t is dropped and then restored.
It is not dropped; it moves.

q: Which stem is the passive of the Aphel?
opts: That is the passive of the Peal.
That is the passive of the Paael.

q: What is the Peal passive participle pattern?
In the story, what happened when Yukhannan was thrown into the furnace?
opts: The fire did not approach him; he was unharmed.
He was badly burned but survived.
The fire did not touch him.
He escaped before being thrown in.

q: Which biblical parallel does the story draw?
opts: Hananiah and his companions in the fiery furnace (Daniel 3)

q: What was seen in the midst of the furnace?
opts: A man of fire was seen.

q: How did the people respond, and what did they say?
opts: Many feared and repented, saying 'Blessed is the God of Yukhannan!' (brīk hū ʾAlāhā d-Yukhannan)
They mocked him, saying 'Where is your God?'

q: Exercise 2. Make passive: malkā qṭal l-gawrā 'the king killed the man'.
opts: The man, not the king, becomes the subject.
That is an Etpaael, and the subject is wrong.

q: Exercise 3. Translate: ܐܬܓܠܝ ܢܘܗܪܐ ܒܚܫܘܟܐ
opts: The light was revealed in the darkness.
The darkness was revealed in the light.

q: Exercise 3. Translate: ܡܫܝܚܐ ܐܬܨܠܒ ܘܐܬܩܒܪ
opts: The Messiah was crucified and buried.
The Messiah was anointed and blessed.
The Messiah prayed and was buried.

q: Exercise 3. Translate: ܐܫܬܡܥ ܩܠܗ ܒܟܠ ܐܬܪ
opts: His voice was heard in every place.
He heard his voice in every place.
His voice was sent to every place.

Exercise 4. Which is the best Syriac for 'The dead man was raised'?
opts: That is active: 'he raised the dead man'.
